Though I can't answer why they put the wiring in there for options that aren't present in the car, I can say that it isnt really all uncommon. All 86+ Fieros are wired to have auxiliary gauges, the connector is in the dash, but they dont all come with them. Same for trunk release, the connector is already under all Fieros' steering columns for the relay.

Fieros that did not come with trunk release came with a 4 wire connector on the car side and then a 3 wire connector on the decklid side. If you had a trunk light, then the 3 wires were for the switch that would then be bolted to the latch assembly. The 4th wire that wouldnt be used on the car side would be the +12v signal for the trunk release. Thats why it is so easy to add trunk release to a car without it, all the wiring is there until you have to fish one wire up the decklid to the soleniod, which isnt that hard. I've added this option to my 87 Coupe.
